messages:
Maya: Heads up — the latest batch of model intakes flagged latency spikes in bench vs runtime. Gap ~15-40ms per prompt. Did we change the adapter contract?
Samir: Not intentionally. Which models? can you paste the bench output?
Maya: See bench-bot output below

bench-bot: ```
model: llama-13b-v3
bench-run: 2024-11-03T14:12Z
median_latency_bench: 48ms
median_latency_runtime: 86ms
kv_cache_warm: false
notes: difference appears only on short-ctx prompts
```
bench-bot: Auto-run finished: 13 models. 2 high-regressions, 7 small diffs, 4 ok. Uploading CSV to /shared/bench/latency-diffs/1729001234.csv
Liam: Short-context diffs smell like tokenization or newline handling. Did the adapter change whitespace normalization in v2?
Dalia: Yes — adapters/v2 did a `strip()` on inputs to normalize training data. That would change prompt length for some tests.
Samir: If `strip()` removed trailing newlines it could reduce prefix caching efficacy (runtime relies on exact prefix match for KV cache). We should add a compatibility flag `adapter.canonicalize_whitespace` and gate it.
Maya: Proposal: onboarding pipeline should perform two validation passes: (A) 'raw parity' — feed inputs unchanged to bench and runtime; (B) 'canonicalized' — with adapter transform applied. Fail if canonicalized changes output semantics but latency regressions > 20%.
Liam: Agree. Also add deterministic seeds for random ops in adapters and models — put `__TEST_SEED=42` in env for bench runs.
Dalia: We need a small manifest field `adapter_compat_level`: `none|soft|strict`. On intake, the validator should compute a diff matrix: tokenization delta, output delta (EM/ROUGE), latency delta.
Samir: We also need to expose KV cache warm-up behavior in the bench harness. Current bench measures cold-start only. Add warm and cold curves: 1, 3, 10 repeated requests for same prefix.
Maya: Operationally, can we add an automatic rollback signal: if runtime p95 latency increases cross-customer by >15% within 1h after deploy, trigger canary->rollback and page oncall.
bench-bot: Quick note: I can start emitting `bench_metadata` header in each run:
```yaml
bench_metadata:
  seed: 42
  warmup_steps: 3
  adapter_flags: [canonicalize_whitespace]
```
Would you like CSV + JSON artifacts?
Dalia: :thumbsup: + yes. Also recommend the pipeline attach a `shim-test` that compares `fast-path` (quantized kernel) vs `reference` (float run) to catch kernel-level regressions.
Liam: Tradeoff: double-run doubles cost. Maybe only run shim-test for large models (>7b) or when adapter_compat_level=strict.
Samir: Implementation plan:
- spec adapter_compat_level in model manifest
- update bench harness to run raw + canonicalized + warm/cold curves
- bench-bot adds metadata and artifacts
- validator emits compatibility matrix and risk score
- console shows per-model latency delta and a toggle to block deploy
I'll draft an RFC.
Maya: Thanks. Quick UX ask: in console can we show the 'cause' label e.g., `tokenization`, `adapter-transform`, `kernel`, `cache-warm`? Makes triage faster.
Samir: Yes — will include in the risk-scoring heuristics.
bench-bot: Artifacts uploading now: https://redwood.internal/bench/1729001234/results.json
Dalia: I'll pick up the adapter flag and manifest change. Samir, can you assign the RFC? I'll add tests.
Samir: Assigned draft RFC to @Samir.aim in drive. Thanks.
